transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because I’ve been feeling really wound up most of the day. It’s like my body is bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner.
Do you find it hard to control the worrying when it starts?

Yes, I do. I’ll try to tell myself, “Daniela, enough, just focus on the report,” but then one thought turns into another and another. Before I realize it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or going over what could go wrong instead of doing what I meant to do.
Did these feelings start after a particular stressful event or major change in your life?

It wasn’t one single event exactly, but it started around thirteen months ago, when my sister in Arecibo began needing a lot more help from the family. That’s when I noticed these feelings really taking hold.
During this time, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed most days. I’ve felt tired and overwhelmed at times, but not really down in that way most of the time.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly about your sister and the family situation?

Yes, it’s more than just my sister. My mind kind of jumps from one thing to the next—her situation, then whether I missed something at work, or my husband driving home, or church things I said I’d do, bills. I’ll catch myself planning for problems that haven’t even happened.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or unusually little need for sleep?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had times where I felt unusually energetic or like I didn’t need sleep. If anything, I usually feel like I need more rest, not less.
Do you often notice your muscles feeling tense or tight?
Yes, I do. I feel kind of wound up almost all day, like my body is bracing for something. Even if I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner, I notice I’m tense.
Has this anxiety been interfering with your day-to-day life?

Yes, somewhat. I’m still getting my work done, and I’m still showing up for my family and church, but it’s taking more effort. Reports take me longer because I keep double-checking things, and I’ve noticed I can sound short with people I care about. I’ve had to apologize for that a few times.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes, I have. Most nights I do fall asleep eventually, but I often wake up around three or four in the morning, thinking about my sister’s next appointment or some server problem at work. And even if I’ve technically had enough hours, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest.
For at least six months, have you been worrying on most days?

Yes. It’s been going on for at least that long. Most days my mind jumps from one worry to the next—my sister in Arecibo, whether I missed something at work, my husband driving home, church things, bills. I catch myself preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying that you might have a serious illness?
No, not really. I don’t usually worry that I have a serious illness myself. My worries tend to be about other things.
